patterns.title: Snowflake curated Import
patterns.summary: Import a governed, dimensional slice. Use incremental refresh for growing fact tables.
patterns.freshness: Bound by source readiness and refresh completion.
patterns.movement: Selected rows are copied into the semantic model.
patterns.licensing: Power BI licensing applies. Model size, refresh limits, and large-model features depend on license/capacity.
chooseWhen: Hours or scheduled batch freshness is sufficient.
Interactive queries should not depend on warehouse availability.
constraints: The imported footprint and peak refresh memory must fit the selected capacity.
Source row policies protect the refresh identity, not each downstream report viewer.
Check current Snowflake driver issues and numeric/timestamp behavior before promotion.
steps: Publish contracted fact/dimension views with explicit SELECT grants.
Select only required columns and date history.
Apply folding RangeStart/RangeEnd filters and an incremental refresh policy.
Publish a shared model, configure connections, test RLS, then release thin reports.
validate: Reconcile amounts, distinct counts, nulls, and date precision with Snowflake.
Inspect the generated source query for partition pruning.
Measure initial and incremental refresh memory, duration, and data age.

focus.security: Reimplement required consumer policies in the semantic model.
focus.cost-optimization: Use a separate BI warehouse; distinguish query-result retrieval from chargeable replication/unload transfer.

patterns.title: Snowflake DirectQuery
patterns.summary: Query curated Snowflake objects on interaction when freshness or detail-copy restrictions justify it.
patterns.freshness: Queries observe source data; report caches and visual refresh still affect visibility.
patterns.movement: Results, metadata, caches, and exports can leave the source. Not a zero-movement architecture.
patterns.licensing: Power BI licensing plus source compute. Entra SSO requires the documented Snowflake integration and identity mapping.
chooseWhen: The business needs source-current queries.
Import is unsuitable after footprint, freshness, and governance assessment.
constraints: Every missed cache/aggregation can consume source compute and network time.
Entra SSO is not enabled simply by using DirectQuery.
Private access requires a supported gateway path; the SaaS service is not inside the source VPC/VNet.
steps: Define the source workload and isolate BI compute.
Configure least-privilege roles and, if selected, Snowflake Entra SSO.
Keep relationships and report interactions bounded; push preparation upstream.
Load-test the actual report with source query history and realistic identities.
validate: Prove effective viewer identity and allowed/denied source rows.
Measure cold/warm p95, warehouse queueing, and concurrent visual fan-out.
Review result caching, export, network policies, and private DNS.

focus.performance-efficiency: Optimize source plans and report query fan-out together.
focus.security: DirectQuery reduces imported detail, but does not establish residency compliance by itself.

patterns.title: Databricks curated Import
patterns.summary: Use a SQL warehouse to serve a curated star schema to incremental Import partitions.
patterns.freshness: Bound by gold-layer completion and semantic-model refresh.
patterns.movement: Curated rows are copied. Cloud Fetch can also read result files from object storage.
patterns.licensing: Power BI licenses/capacity plus Databricks SQL compute. Authentication and connector choice vary by cloud.
chooseWhen: A curated subset meets reporting needs.
Batch freshness and predictable interactive query behavior are appropriate.
constraints: Do not point enterprise report traffic at an interactive all-purpose engineering cluster by default.
Verify connector/authentication support separately for Azure, AWS, and GCP.
Warehouse endpoint reachability alone is insufficient when Cloud Fetch also uses protected storage.
steps: Publish a stable gold-layer schema with explicit grain and column types.
Grant the BI identity only required catalog/schema/table and warehouse access.
Select the documented cloud/auth connector and validate date-filter folding.
Publish shared semantics and release reports independently.
validate: Compare source totals and measure date/decimal conversions.
Test result-storage access for large queries as well as small queries.
Measure incremental refresh pruning, memory, duration, and source compute.

focus.operational-excellence: Version the curated SQL contract and test schema changes.
focus.security: A storage shortcut is not a substitute for this SQL authorization boundary.

patterns.title: Databricks SQL DirectQuery
patterns.summary: Serve source-current queries through a tuned SQL warehouse, not an assumed low-latency cross-cloud path.
patterns.freshness: Query-time source visibility; caches and visual refresh remain relevant.
patterns.movement: Query results and possible Cloud Fetch files cross the connection boundary.
patterns.licensing: Power BI licensing plus SQL warehouse compute; verify supported workload identity or viewer SSO for the chosen connector/cloud.
chooseWhen: Fresh detail cannot wait for scheduled Import.
Source engineering can own BI concurrency and query-plan tuning.
constraints: Do not generalize the AWS OAuth connector to GCP; follow both current Microsoft and cloud-specific Databricks requirements.
Cloud Fetch can require additional object-storage network access.
Auto-stop/start and source queues can change cold-query behavior.
steps: Create a dedicated, governed SQL serving path.
Validate the selected connector and effective identity in Desktop and the service.
Use star-schema views, selective filters, and restrained report interactions.
Observe SQL query history and Power BI capacity together under load.
validate: Test the exact authentication flow after publishing and through any gateway.
Run cold-start and warmed warehouse concurrency tests.
Inspect query fan-out, Cloud Fetch reachability, and data-leakage boundaries.

focus.performance-efficiency: Measure source startup, queues, execution, and result download separately.
focus.security: Use SQL/Unity Catalog policy enforcement only where the selected identity actually applies.

patterns.title: Import aggregates + DirectQuery detail
patterns.summary: Keep common summaries in memory and route eligible drill-through queries to source detail.
patterns.freshness: Aggregate refresh cadence and detail query time differ.
patterns.movement: Aggregated rows are imported; detail results can also move.
patterns.licensing: Manual aggregation modeling and capacity sizing apply. Automatic aggregations have separate capacity requirements.
chooseWhen: Most interactions can be answered at a much smaller grain.
Detailed drill-through is selective and source queries are acceptable.
constraints: Imported aggregates still need residency and policy approval.
Aggregation mappings, relationships, and security must preserve equivalent answers.
An aggregation miss returns to DirectQuery and its source costs.
steps: Measure common report groupings and select an aggregate grain.
Create a contracted aggregate table or view.
Import the aggregate, configure Manage aggregations, and review dimension storage modes.
Validate query routing and reconciled answers with and without aggregation hits.
validate: Compare totals and distinct-count semantics across hit/miss paths.
Verify RLS on both aggregate and detail paths.
Measure hit ratio, cold/warm p95, and source workload reduction.

focus.performance-efficiency: Prove an aggregation hit; adding a summary table alone does not configure routing.
focus.reliability: Show when summary and detail represent different refresh times.

patterns.title: Historical Import + hot DirectQuery
patterns.summary: Partition historical data in Import mode and use a DirectQuery partition for the latest interval.
patterns.freshness: Historical partitions follow policy; the hot partition is queried at the source.
patterns.movement: Historical detail is imported and hot-query results move.
patterns.licensing: The real-time DirectQuery partition requires a supported Premium, PPU, or Embedded configuration; verify the current feature/license matrix.
chooseWhen: Historical queries dominate but the latest interval needs query-time access.
A single supported source can serve the table's partitions.
constraints: Incremental refresh alone does not enable the real-time partition.
Range boundaries, time zones, and late-arriving corrections need explicit design.
A hot DirectQuery partition still depends on source availability and performance.
steps: Define case-sensitive RangeStart and RangeEnd Date/Time parameters.
Apply a half-open, foldable filter to the fact date/time column.
Configure history, refresh window, and the optional real-time setting.
Publish, complete initial refresh, and inspect partition behavior.
validate: Test boundary rows for missing or duplicate records.
Exercise late corrections inside and outside the refresh window.
Inspect source predicates and cold/warm hot-partition query latency.

focus.reliability: Define how old corrections are detected and reprocessed.
focus.performance-efficiency: Measure the hot partition; its small size does not guarantee low source latency.

patterns.title: Snowflake mirroring + Direct Lake
patterns.summary: Use supported Fabric mirroring to expose Snowflake data through OneLake, then model with Direct Lake.
patterns.freshness: Asynchronous, object-specific propagation. Current documentation lists 12-hour view/materialized-view syncs.
patterns.movement: Managed-table data is replicated. Supported Iceberg objects use underlying storage connections/shortcuts; review per object.
patterns.licensing: Fabric capacity plus Power BI author/consumer licensing. Source mirroring compute, storage, and transfer must be assessed.
chooseWhen: An approved OneLake/Fabric serving layer is part of the target estate.
Supported objects and observed replication lag meet the data contract.
constraints: This is not Direct Lake directly querying an arbitrary Snowflake SQL endpoint.
Do not assume row/masking policies are reproduced in the copied model.
Verify current object, authentication, private-connectivity, table-count, and region limitations.
steps: Classify each selected object as managed table, supported Iceberg table, or other supported type.
Approve replication/storage access and configure least-privilege mirror credentials.
Validate the OneLake representation and select the appropriate Direct Lake variant.
Define semantic permissions, freshness alerts, and operating ownership.
validate: Reconcile rows, schema changes, deletes, and recovery behavior.
Measure observed lag for each source object type, not only a single table.
Test semantic RLS and distinguish Direct Lake on OneLake from SQL fallback behavior.

focus.security: Source governance is not automatically inherited by every downstream engine.
focus.cost-optimization: Separate managed-table replication costs from the Snowflake query-result egress exception.

patterns.title: External Delta shortcuts + Direct Lake
patterns.summary: Reference eligible ADLS, S3, or GCS Delta paths from a Fabric lakehouse rather than building an unmanaged replica.
patterns.freshness: Depends on source commits, table discovery, metadata propagation, and model framing.
patterns.movement: No separately managed source replica is required; remote reads, caching, and result movement still occur.
patterns.licensing: Fabric capacity and Power BI licensing; storage transactions and cross-cloud transfer may be billed.
chooseWhen: The approved data product exposes a supported storage/table-format contract.
Storage-level authorization is intentionally sufficient for the consuming workload.
constraints: A shortcut does not execute Databricks SQL or automatically enforce Unity Catalog row/column policies.
An arbitrary Parquet folder is not automatically a valid Direct Lake table.
Validate Delta features, cloud credentials, caching, and format compatibility.
steps: Publish an approved, stable Delta data product and supported protocol features.
Scope the storage credential to the intended path.
Create a Tables shortcut and verify successful table discovery.
Create Direct Lake semantics and implement consumer policy at the correct engine.
validate: Test schema/protocol evolution and source path changes.
Prove source storage permissions and semantic allowed/denied behavior.
Measure remote reads, caching, transferred bytes, and end-to-end freshness.

focus.security: Treat direct file access as a distinct authorization path.
focus.cost-optimization: No replica does not mean no network transfer or no charges.

patterns.title: Azure Databricks catalog mirroring
patterns.summary: Mirror eligible Unity Catalog metadata into Fabric; read the underlying data through shortcuts.
patterns.freshness: Metadata/data visibility is asynchronous; measure source commit to report visibility.
patterns.movement: Catalog metadata is mirrored, not a managed-table data replica. Reads still access underlying storage.
patterns.licensing: Fabric capacity, Power BI licensing, and accessible supported ADLS storage are prerequisites.
chooseWhen: Azure Databricks and Fabric share an approved storage-access design.
Selected tables fit the documented catalog-mirroring eligibility rules.
constraints: This Azure Databricks feature is not an AWS/GCP Databricks catalog-mirroring promise.
Current limitations exclude tables with RLS/column-mask policies, views, streaming tables, and other listed types.
Underlying ADLS must be reachable by Fabric.
steps: Inventory eligible catalogs/tables and source policy dependencies.
Review supported regions, storage access, and table exclusions.
Select catalog/schema/table scope; review automatic future-table inclusion.
Build the Direct Lake model and independently validate downstream permissions.
validate: Verify excluded/policy-protected tables cannot enter the intended path.
Test catalog/table additions and removal propagation.
Reconcile query answers and measure framing/metadata delay.

focus.security: Do not bypass an unsupported Unity Catalog policy by granting broad file access.
focus.operational-excellence: Treat automatic future-table discovery as a governed scope change.

patterns.title: Consolidated curated serving layer
patterns.summary: Integrate approved data upstream, resolve shared dimensions once, and serve a coherent model.
patterns.freshness: Pipeline SLA plus serving-layer and model visibility.
patterns.movement: Approved data is copied/transformed into a selected serving region.
patterns.licensing: Existing warehouse/lakehouse and integration costs; Fabric capacity is needed only for a Fabric/Direct Lake implementation.
chooseWhen: Cross-source joins, data quality, or shared dimensions are a core requirement.
Approved replication is preferable to repeated interactive cross-cloud joins.
constraints: Residency, deletion, lineage, and transfer cost must be approved before copying.
Consolidation does not require migrating every source table.
The source-of-truth contract and handling of late data must remain explicit.
steps: Define shared business keys, grain, currency, and time-zone rules.
Choose the approved serving region and minimum required source columns/history.
Build reconciled incremental ingestion and conformed dimensions.
Expose governed semantics and reusable thin reports.
validate: Reconcile cross-system keys, totals, late changes, and duplicate handling.
Test freshness and restartability at each pipeline boundary.
Measure full cost and consumer concurrency at the serving layer.

focus.performance-efficiency: Resolve expensive joins upstream instead of per visual.
focus.reliability: Observe ingestion, serving data, and semantic refresh as separate stages.

patterns.title: Governed Delta Sharing Import
patterns.summary: Consume a bounded provider-published share through the documented Power Query sharing connector.
patterns.freshness: Bound by share availability and consumer refresh cadence.
patterns.movement: Shared rows are copied into the consumer semantic model.
patterns.licensing: Power BI licensing plus the provider's sharing and storage/transfer arrangement.
chooseWhen: Provider and consumer need an explicit sharing contract.
The shared slice fits a governed Import workload.
constraints: The Microsoft Delta Sharing connector documents Import only.
The documented default row limit is 1,000,000; explicitly validate scope and completeness.
Sharing credentials must not be committed into PBIX/PBIP source or scripts.
steps: Agree recipient identity, approved tables, retention, and revocation behavior.
Configure the current documented sharing authentication method.
Set an intentional row limit and validate the extracted scope.
Apply consumer semantic controls and a refresh/credential runbook.
validate: Compare imported row counts and totals with the provider contract.
Test credential expiry/revocation and the impact on refresh.
Verify consumer RLS, export settings, and deletion obligations.

focus.reliability: A revoked share stops future reads, not necessarily existing consumer copies.
focus.security: Treat imported copies and their retention as part of the sharing agreement.

patterns.title: Shared semantics + thin reports
patterns.summary: Separate centrally owned semantic models from domain-owned report experiences.
patterns.freshness: Inherited from the shared model's underlying storage/refresh design.
patterns.movement: Determined by the model's Import, DirectQuery, hybrid, or Direct Lake design.
patterns.licensing: Author/consumer licensing and Build permission depend on the sharing and capacity arrangement.
chooseWhen: Many report creators need consistent measures and security.
Citizen developers should focus on reports rather than duplicate data pipelines.
constraints: A live connection to a semantic model is not DirectQuery to Snowflake/Databricks.
Build permission and elevated workspace roles need explicit review.
A report's presentation filter is not a security boundary.
steps: Assign an accountable model owner and measure/data contract.
Publish the model independently of report workspaces.
Provide reviewed Build access to authors and Viewer/app access to consumers.
Document extension, endorsement, change, and deprecation processes.
validate: Confirm two reports produce the same governed measures.
Test actual Viewer identities and elevated-role exceptions.
Exercise model change impact, lineage, rollback, and owner handover.

focus.operational-excellence: Promote model and report changes through separate ownership workflows.
focus.security: RLS does not constrain workspace Admin, Member, or Contributor roles.

patterns.title: Private-source gateway path
patterns.summary: Place a supported gateway where it can resolve and reach private source and result-storage endpoints.
patterns.freshness: Determined by the consuming model; gateway placement does not define storage mode.
patterns.movement: Import rows or query results traverse the gateway according to the selected model.
patterns.licensing: Standard gateway hosts incur operational costs. VNet data gateways require a documented eligible capacity and supported region.
chooseWhen: Source policy requires private endpoint access.
The selected connector and gateway authentication combination is supported.
constraints: A private endpoint alone does not give the Power BI service a route to the source.
A VNet gateway is not a VPN gateway; cross-cloud routing and private DNS still need design.
Dedicated network connectivity is not automatically encrypted; AWS Direct Connect is not encrypted by default.
steps: Choose standard versus VNet gateway using connector, region, identity, and capacity requirements.
Design DNS, private endpoint resolution, routing, and result-storage reachability.
For VNet gateways, delegate a dedicated subnet to Microsoft.PowerPlatform/vnetaccesslinks.
Test actual service queries and establish gateway monitoring/recovery ownership.
validate: Resolve private names and test warehouse plus Cloud Fetch storage traffic.
Prove TLS and any required IPsec/MACsec design for the actual route.
Test failover/member loss and verify no unintended public fallback.

focus.security: Prove the complete route rather than assuming the word private covers every hop.
focus.reliability: Gateway HA protects a gateway failure, not the source or the entire BI service.

patterns.title: Bounded cross-source composite
patterns.summary: Combine a small number of controlled source groups when upstream integration is not justified.
patterns.freshness: Each source group follows its own query/refresh semantics.
patterns.movement: Intermediate results and any imported tables cross boundaries.
patterns.licensing: Power BI licensing, remote-model permissions where relevant, and compute at each queried source.
chooseWhen: Join keys and dimensions are small, controlled, and benchmarked.
A bounded extension is cheaper to operate than a new integrated data product.
constraints: High-cardinality cross-source fact joins can materialize large intermediates and amplify latency.
Separate source groups can produce different freshness and security semantics.
Remote semantic-model chaining has documented restrictions; it is not unlimited federation.
steps: Inventory source groups, identities, relationship keys, and query boundaries.
Keep cross-source relationships narrow; avoid fact-to-fact joins.
Document each group's freshness and consumer policy behavior.
Benchmark intended interactions and set an explicit redesign threshold.
validate: Inspect emitted source queries and intermediate-result behavior.
Test RLS and relationship semantics using real consumer roles.
Compare p95, source credits, and reliability with an upstream-conformed alternative.

focus.performance-efficiency: Reject the design if realistic cardinality/concurrency fails, even if a small demo works.
focus.reliability: A single report can now depend on multiple source availability domains.

patterns.title: On-premises integration + gateway HA
patterns.summary: Connect supported on-premises systems through a managed standard gateway cluster, then choose Import or DirectQuery.
patterns.freshness: Chosen model or upstream pipeline cadence; not a property of gateway HA.
patterns.movement: Selected rows or query results leave on-premises; approve their destination.
patterns.licensing: Power BI/integration licensing plus Windows hosts, patching, and operations.
chooseWhen: The estate includes supported sources behind on-premises network boundaries.
Enterprise availability and non-personal operational ownership are required.
constraints: Personal mode is not the enterprise HA standard.
Keep cluster members on consistent supported versions.
The source connector determines DirectQuery support; the gateway does not add it.
steps: Assign gateway administrators and securely retain the recovery key.
Install standard gateway members on dedicated managed hosts.
Configure source identity, connections, outbound network access, and monitoring.
Select curated Import or a justified DirectQuery path and test member loss.
validate: Stop a gateway member during a controlled test and observe service behavior.
Measure host resources, source locks/queues, and refresh concurrency.
Restore/recover the cluster using the documented owner and recovery procedure.

focus.reliability: Test gateway and source failure independently.
focus.operational-excellence: Treat patching, recovery keys, and connection ownership as platform operations.

patterns.title: Region-scoped BI estates
patterns.summary: Keep separately governed regional models when central row-level consolidation is not approved.
patterns.freshness: A regional data contract; summaries may have a separate release cadence.
patterns.movement: Only explicitly approved results/summaries may cross regions. Separate models alone do not prove residency.
patterns.licensing: Review tenant/capacity location, author/consumer access, and operational duplication.
chooseWhen: Legal or contractual constraints prevent central row-level data pooling.
Regional owners can operate independently under common contracts.
constraints: Report viewing, caches, exports, support access, and metadata may still cross boundaries.
A single global report is not automatically permitted.
Cross-tenant identity, tenant home region, and capacity placement require separate review.
steps: Have legal/data governance define the permitted data and access boundaries.
Map tenant, capacity, source, gateway, consumer, and metadata locations.
Deploy region-specific semantic contracts and controlled report access.
Publish only explicitly approved cross-region summaries or links.
validate: Review actual network/data flows, caches, downloads, and support procedures.
Test regional access denials and summary disclosure controls.
Exercise region-specific recovery without unapproved failover destinations.

focus.security: Require a signed data-flow assessment; this pattern is not a compliance guarantee.
focus.cost-optimization: Budget duplicated operations and capacity rather than hiding regional overhead.

antipatterns.title: DirectQuery because the source is large
antipatterns.symptom: Every visual queries a multi-terabyte source before workload testing.
antipatterns.risk: Source queueing, query fan-out, variable latency, and compute spend.
antipatterns.instead: Start with the required grain and freshness; evaluate Import, aggregates, or an approved lake path.

antipatterns.title: Interactive cross-cloud fact-to-fact joins
antipatterns.symptom: A report joins large Snowflake and Databricks fact tables across source groups.
antipatterns.risk: Large intermediate results, expensive source queries, and coupled outages.
antipatterns.instead: Conform data upstream, or deliberately bound and benchmark the composite model.

antipatterns.title: Shortcuts as a Unity Catalog policy bypass
antipatterns.symptom: Direct file access is granted to reproduce a policy-protected SQL table.
antipatterns.risk: Row filters and column masks may not apply on the alternate engine path.
antipatterns.instead: Use a supported SQL policy path or publish a separately approved data product.

antipatterns.title: Calling DirectQuery or shortcuts zero movement
antipatterns.symptom: Results, caches, storage reads, or exports are omitted from the data-flow review.
antipatterns.risk: Residency violations and incomplete cost estimates.
antipatterns.instead: Model each row, result, cache, metadata, and export boundary explicitly.

antipatterns.title: Enterprise refresh on a personal laptop
antipatterns.symptom: One person's machine, credentials, or gateway is the production dependency.
antipatterns.risk: Unmanaged outages, credential expiry, and no recovery ownership.
antipatterns.instead: Use a managed standard gateway cluster or eligible VNet gateway.

antipatterns.title: Report filters instead of authorization
antipatterns.symptom: Hidden columns, slicers, or page filters are treated as row security.
antipatterns.risk: Other reports, exports, Build access, or elevated roles can expose data.
antipatterns.instead: Test source and semantic authorization using actual consumer identities.

antipatterns.title: Mirroring assumed to preserve every policy
antipatterns.symptom: Copied data is released without checking object eligibility or downstream RLS.
antipatterns.risk: Unsupported table types, stale views, or broader consumer access.
antipatterns.instead: Classify mirrored objects and revalidate permissions and freshness.

antipatterns.title: Private endpoint assumed to complete networking
antipatterns.symptom: Warehouse DNS resolves somewhere, but gateway routes, TLS, or result storage are untested.
antipatterns.risk: Small tests pass while large queries fail; traffic takes an unintended route.
antipatterns.instead: Prove service-to-gateway-to-source and Cloud Fetch paths end-to-end.
